title: Solomon Becomes King
summary: As David grows old, Adonijah declares himself king with the backing of Joab and Abiathar. Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his promise, and Solomon is anointed at Gihon, while Adonijah flees to the altar. David charges Solomon to keep the law and to settle accounts with Joab and Shimei, then dies after forty years. Solomon later has Adonijah, Joab and Shimei put to death and removes Abiathar, and the kingdom is established.

title: Solomon's Wisdom
summary: Solomon marries Pharaoh's daughter and sacrifices at the high place of Gibeon, where God appears in a dream and offers him anything. Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people, and God adds riches and honor. Two women who share a house each claim a living baby; Solomon proposes cutting it in two, and the true mother gives it up. The chapter lists his officials and says his wisdom surpassed that of the east and Egypt, with 3,000 proverbs and 1,005 songs.

title: The Temple Built
summary: Solomon asks Hiram of Tyre for cedar and fir and, with forced labor and thousands of workers, begins the temple in his fourth year and finishes it in seven. He also builds his own palace. The ark is brought into the inner room, and a cloud fills the house so that the priests cannot minister. Solomon blesses the people, prays at the dedication that God will hear prayers toward the house, and offers thousands of sacrifices in a feast of fourteen days.

title: The Queen of Sheba and Solomon's Decline
summary: God appears to Solomon again, promising to establish his throne if he walks faithfully and warning of exile if he turns away. The queen of Sheba comes to test him with hard questions, is amazed at his wisdom and house, and gives gifts of gold and spices. But Solomon loves many foreign women, who turn his heart to other gods. God raises up adversaries, and the prophet Ahijah tells Jeroboam he will rule ten tribes. Solomon dies after forty years.

title: The Kingdom Divides
summary: At Shechem the people ask Rehoboam to lighten his father's heavy yoke. Rehoboam rejects the elders' advice for his young friends' and answers that his father chastised them with whips but he will use scorpions. The ten northern tribes make Jeroboam king, and Rehoboam's labor chief Adoram is stoned. Jeroboam, fearing the people will return to Jerusalem, makes two golden calves at Beth-el and Dan, appoints priests from outside Levi, and sets a feast.

title: The Man of God from Judah
summary: A man of God from Judah cries out against Jeroboam's altar at Beth-el, the altar splits, and the king's withered hand is healed at his prayer. He refuses the king's invitation to eat, but an old prophet at Beth-el claims an angel told him to bring him back; the man of God eats with him and is killed by a lion on the road. Ahijah later foretells the end of Jeroboam's house, and in Rehoboam's reign Shishak of Egypt takes the temple treasures.

title: Kings of Judah and Israel
summary: The text moves quickly through the kings of Judah and Israel. Abijam is unfaithful; Asa removes idols but later pays Ben-hadad of Syria to attack Baasha of Israel. In the north Nadab is killed by Baasha, and Elah by Zimri, who reigns seven days before Omri takes power and builds Samaria. Omri's son Ahab marries Jezebel of Sidon and serves Baal, and Hiel rebuilds Jericho at the cost of his sons.

title: Elijah and the Drought
summary: Elijah the Tishbite tells Ahab there will be no rain or dew except at his word, then hides by the brook Cherith, where ravens bring him bread and meat. When the brook dries, God sends him to a widow at Zarephath, whose handful of flour and little oil last until the drought ends. Her son dies, and Elijah stretches himself on the child three times and prays, and the boy lives. The widow says the word of the LORD in his mouth is truth.

title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
summary: In the third year of the drought Elijah meets Obadiah, who has hidden 100 prophets from Jezebel, and tells Ahab to gather Israel and 450 prophets of Baal at Carmel. Elijah asks how long they will limp between two opinions. The prophets of Baal call from morning until evening without answer; Elijah rebuilds the LORD's altar, drenches it with water, and prays, and fire falls and consumes the offering. The people cry 'The LORD, he is the God', the prophets are killed at Kishon, and rain comes.

title: Elijah at Horeb
summary: Threatened by Jezebel, Elijah flees to Beer-sheba and a day further, asking to die under a juniper tree, where an angel feeds him. Strengthened, he goes forty days to Horeb and says he alone is left. The LORD passes: wind, earthquake and fire, but he is not in them, and then a still small voice. Elijah is sent to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha and told that seven thousand have not bowed to Baal. He throws his mantle over Elisha, who follows him.

title: Naboth's Vineyard
summary: Ahab wants Naboth's vineyard beside his palace at Jezreel, but Naboth refuses to sell his ancestral land. Ahab sulks, and Jezebel writes letters in his name arranging for two false witnesses to accuse Naboth of cursing God and the king; Naboth is stoned. When Ahab goes to take the vineyard, Elijah meets him and announces that dogs will lick his blood and eat Jezebel. Ahab humbles himself, and God delays the disaster until his son's days.

title: Ahab and Micaiah
summary: After three years of peace, Ahab asks Jehoshaphat of Judah to join him against Syria at Ramoth-gilead. Four hundred prophets promise victory, but Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet of the LORD, and Micaiah son of Imlah says he saw Israel scattered like sheep and a lying spirit sent to Ahab's prophets. Ahab jails him and goes into battle disguised; an arrow shot at random strikes him between the joints of his armor, and he dies. The chapter closes with Jehoshaphat and Ahab's son Ahaziah.
